answer.rationale: Write-path p99 at 5x coincides with daily settlement peak and heavy writes; the objective is sustained availability without dropping customer writes. enable_circuit_breaker is rejected because failing fast on the write path would shed writes (memory_b4 is a partner-outage lesson, not a write-shedding license). route_read_replicas is a weak fit: memory_b5 recovered write latency by offloading report/dashboard reads, but the stated load here is settlement writes. regional_failover has no regional signal. Rollback (memory_b1) remains a live alternate cause because a release shipped two hours ago, but the climb over 90 minutes also matches a peak ramp and rollback is not required to explain the symptom. memory_b3 is the closest positive lesson—headroom absorbed a peak without queue growth—so add_capacity is the intended single intervention, applied broadly enough to matter at 5x p99. Verifying memory_b3 because the summary describes provisioning before a peak, not mid-incident scale-up; that gap is material and is not assumed away.
